newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Fatal mine accident cause unclear - Oakbridge.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Fatal mine accident cause unclear - Oakbridge.

text.p: Oakbridge Pty Ltd did not know the cause of the accident at Gretley colliery in the Hunter Valley of New South Wales which killed four miners, the company said in a statement.
The present focus was on recovery of the victims and assistance of their families, it said.

"At this point the company does not know the cause of the accident and will not speculate on the cause until investigations of the various authorities and of the company are completed," the statement said.
Newcastle police earlier told Reuters that the accident was caused when miners broke into old workings, causing floodwaters to break through into the area they were working 120 metres underground.

The mine in the Hunter Valley, Australia's second largest coal district, is owned by Oakbridge Ltd. Oakbridge is 42-percent owned by the U.S. Cyprus Amax mining group, the second largest coal producer in the United States, which has been expanding its coal operations in Australia.
The accident occurred at 5.30 am (1830 GMT), when the mine's emergency response procedures were immediately activated and external emergency rescue authorities called in, it said.
"The incident occurred when a team was conducting mining operations," the Oakbridge statement said.
Water entered the mine and four people were killed but no explosion was involved, the statement said.
Colliery management was cooperating fully with authorities and also working with Mines Rescue and police to investigate the cause of the accident, it said.
The company will conduct its own investigation, it said.
